title: How A “Mysterious” Message Kickstarted Aardman’s Gamechanging Pact With Pokémon
full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Biggest ITV Shows Like ‘Love Island’ & ‘I’m A Celebrity’ To Remain Free-To-Air Once Sky Deal Completes BBC Deputy Boss Questions Impact Of “Creative Choices Taken On West Coast Of United States” On UK Audiences Melissa George Leading BBC-BritBox Detective Series ‘The Loch Ness Mysteries’ View All November 19, 2026 5:22am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Aardman and The Pokemon Company are collaborating on a special project Lionsgate/Warner Bros/Everett Collection It was a “mysterious” message that kickstarted Aardman ’s once-in-a-generation team-up with Pokémon. The celebrated stop motion outfit’s creative chief talked a London audience through the inception of Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu , which lands next year on Disney+. The pact represents Aardman’s first time taking its stop motion approach to a third party brand. “They approached us surreptitiously at Annecy [International Animation Film Festival],” Sarah Cox said today at the British Screen Forum Conference. “It was a mysterious message saying, ‘Would you like to take a phone call from this person?’.” Related Stories News UK Culture Minister Delivers Emotional Plea To YouTube To "Set An Example" & Remove Russell Brand's Channel News Tilly Norwood Creator Teases Next Project 'Storm Dogs' & Shows Clip Pokémon gave Aardman carte blanche to do what it wanted with the characters. The result, Pokémon Tales , places its heroes front and centre in a region Trainers have explored before, Aardman says. Watch on Deadline “The first conversation we had was not about the project or animation, it was about our values and the value of wanting to deliver really good meaningful content to our audiences,” said Cox. “We want strong characters, strong humor and a commitment to the quality of what we do. We talked for a while and the project emerged from those discussions.” Pokémon Tales launches next year on Disney+ via the Mouse House’s partnership with Pokémon. Aardman MD Sean Clarke said “taking on other people’s brands” will help the 50-year-old, employee-owned outfit navigate an independent production landscape that is struggling, especially when Aardman prides itself on protecting its “integrity” by only releasing Wallace & Gromit movies once every five years or so. Another way in which Aardman is doing this is by embracing TikTok, with a bespoke Shaun the Sheep video going viral earlier this week that poked fun at James Bond. “If we are here three years from now I would hope we have launched new characters doing funny things on TikTok so we can then go to market,” added Clarke. “At the moment you go to market to try and raise money and it’s all prequels, sequels and remakes. So this gives you a different ability to raise money.” Aardman may be embracing TikTok but it is incredibly wary of AI. “When I look at AI it all looks the same because it’s learning from stuff that already exists,” added Clarke. “Why would we want to change what we do?” Elsewhere, Clarke echoed concerns raised earlier today by culture minister Ian Murray that the proposed U.S. federal film and TV tax incentive will negatively impact UK production. According to Clarke, there were zero independent British animations launched last year, compared to around 10 in France and 15 in Germany. Clarke added: “The bulk of the [UK] film and TV industry is making things for others and when you have Americans saying, ‘Maybe we should look at our own tax credit,’ then you have a real issue with less things being made in this country versus having an ecosystem to retain rights.” Earlier, Murray said the UK government is taking the implications of the proposed credit “incredibly seriously.” The Aardman bosses were speaking at the British Screen Forum Conference in London after Tilly Norwood creator Eline Van der Velden and Murray. title: Melissa George Leading BBC-BritBox Detective Series ‘The Loch Ness Mysteries’
full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Biggest ITV Shows Like ‘Love Island’ & ‘I’m A Celebrity’ To Remain Free-To-Air Once Sky Deal Completes BBC Deputy Boss Questions Impact Of “Creative Choices Taken On West Coast Of United States” On UK Audiences Melissa George Leading BBC-BritBox Detective Series ‘The Loch Ness Mysteries’ View All November 19, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L to R: Jamie Sives, Melissa George, Ashley Storrie Nobby Clark, Angelo Buonomo and Didier Cometti EXCLUSIVE: Mosquito Coast star Melissa George is leading a BBC and BritBox detective series set around Scotland’s most famous mystery. The Loch Ness Mysteries also stars Jamie Sives ( Dept Q ) and Ashley Storrie ( Dinosaur ). George is DCI Vanessa ‘Nessie’ Keen, a provocative London detective whose life is thrown off course when a brush with death leaves her signed off work and persona non grata, until a peculiar personal mystery summons her to the shores of Loch Ness. From Scotland Yard to Scotland, Nessie arrives in the remote Highland district of Monaruadh, only to find herself drawn into a dark and perplexing case alongside local detective DS Rory Ramsay (Sives), whose knowledge of the idiosyncratic local community prove as valuable as Nessie’s razor-sharp instincts. Despite their different approaches and clashes, the two have an undeniable chemistry, forming a duo alongside PC Donna Duff (Storrie). Further casting will be announced in due course. Related Stories News Harry Styles, Billie Eilish & Sam Fender To Headline Glastonbury 2027 News 'Dancing With The Stars' Finale Will Go Live Across The Country For The First Time The six-part series derives its name from the notorious monster, also known as Nessie, a mythical creature in Scottish folklore said to inhabit the Scottish Highlands. It is created and led by writer Ed Sellek ( Sister Boniface Mysteries ) and comes from Deborah Sathe’s nascent BBC Studios -backed label CliffEdge Entertainment, which is already making The Detection Club for the BBC and BritBox. Watch on Deadline George is an Australian star of Apple TV’s The Mosquito Coast , ABC’s Alias and NBC’s The Slap. She was Golden Globe nominated for playing Laura Hill in HBO’s In Treatment. George said: “Rarely do stories like this come across, with a brilliant and developed character like Nessie. I was immediately drawn to this world and it has been a joy to have a hand in shaping it. I cannot wait to step into these shoes and get on set.” Sellek added: “I couldn’t be more stoked for the wickedly talented cast and crew we’re assembling for this show. It’s a murderer’s row of great performers, writers and a production team that’s second-to-none. I think we’re building something really special here.” The Loch Ness Mysteries (6×48) was commissioned by Louise Thornton for the BBC and Jon Farrar for BritBox. George is an EP on the show outside the UK and Ireland. Other EPs are Gavin Smith for the BBC, Sathe and Sarah Creasey for CliffEdge and Stephen Nye for BritBox. The six-part series is created and led by Sellek with additional episodes written by Scottish writers Ciara Conway ( The Teacher 3 ) and Niki Rooney ( Malory Towers ). Katherine Churcher ( Grantchester ) is directing the first block of filming with subsequent episodes directed by Brian Kelly ( No Way Off ) and Ryan Graham ( River City ). The series producer is Kevin McComiskie, known for his work on River City . BBC Studios is handling global sales. Filming will begin before the end of year around the Luss and Glasgow areas. George is repped by Conway Van Gelder Grant, Inspire Entertainment and GGSSC.
